learning_outcomes.text: To have knowledge and understanding of the fundamentals of automatisms and control methods.
To be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve problems related to industrial automation using established methods.
To be able to apply their knowledge to develop and carry out the design of industrial automation systems that meet specific requirements.
To be able to design and conduct experiments, interpret data and draw conclusions.
To have technical and laboratory competences.
To select and use appropriate equipment, tools and methods.
To combine theory and practice to solve industrial automation problems.
A systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects of their engineering field.
Awareness of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems using established methods.
The ability to design and conduct experiments, interpret data and draw conclusions.
The ability to select and use appropriate equipment, tools and methods.
The ability to combine theory and practice to solve engineering problems.

That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences typically demonstrated through the development and defense of arguments and problem-solving within their field of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to design and conduct experiments and to analyze and interpret the data obtained.
Knowledge about the fundamentals of automatisms and control methods.

syllabus_topics: Presentation and introduction to the course.
Definition of the concept of industrial automation.
Historical introduction.
Distinction between discrete and continuous event systems.
Modeling of discrete event systems: State diagrams and SFC.
Review of basic concepts of Boolean algebra.
Definition of sequential systems. Concept of states.
Modeling with graphical representations of sequential systems.
Modeling with State Diagrams. Problem sessions are held.
Modeling with Petri Nets. Basic concepts.
Modeling with Sequential Function Chart (SFC). Problem sessions are held.
Introduction to technologies used in automation: programmable logic controllers or PLCs and their hardware architecture.
PLC programming languages:
Ladder Diagram language. Problem sessions are held to program with LD from a State Diagram model.
Programming with Sequential Function Chart (SFC) and LD. Problem sessions are held.
Introduction to actuators:
Basic concepts of electric motors.
Basic concepts of hydraulic actuators.
Basic concepts of pneumatics.
Introduction to sensors:
Characteristics and classification.
Description of sensors by measured quantity.
Introduction to industrial communications: fieldbuses.
teaching_methods: Resolution of exercises by the student
assessment_rules: A minimum grade of 3 in the final exam is required to pass the course.
